newsitem.title: USA: Montana Power files deregulation plan.
newsitem.headline: Montana Power files deregulation plan.

text.p: Montana Power Co said Monday it filed an "informational plan" with state regulators to restructure the utility's electricity business.
The company's plan includes phasing in direct access for all Montana consumers by July 1, 2002.

Dean Conklin, a spokesman for Montana Power, said the plan suggests starting a pilot program on July 1, 1998, which would include 3,000 residential customers and 1,000 commercial customers with industrial customers able to purchase up to one-third of their electric load from other suppliers.
Those numbers would rise in 2000 to 25,000 residential, 5,000 commercial and two-third of industrial loads.
"We don't wish to start a formal docket until the Montana Legislature has met and reviewed electric restructuring issues," noted Robert Gannon, Montana Power's president.
-- Allowing generation assets to compete in the market.
-- Safety and reliability, with the expectation that Montana's Public Service Commission would continue to regulate the monopoly distribution system.
-- A "universal systems benefits charge" to cover low-income services and energy efficiency programs.
-- Competitive transition charges to cover costs for investments and expenditures utilities were required by law to make, such as contracts to buy electricity from qualifying facilities.
